subject: Quick recap + one-question: who owns HorizonHealth's budget window?
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from discovery — quick question on budget owner

Alex — thanks for carving out time this morning. Quick recap of the 30m:
- Use case: internal search & clinical summarization for HorizonHealth patient ops (pilot scope: 4 clinics, ~1500 monthly active encounters).
- Key constraints: latency <= 300ms p50, data residency in us-west, and audit logs required.
- Pilot ask: 3-month trial, then production roll in Q3 if metrics look good.

Only one quick clarifying question before I lock in the MAP: who at HorizonHealth owns the approval/budget for this work? You mentioned "finance + clinical ops" — can you confirm the primary approver (name/email) and whether the decision window is still end-of-quarter?

Next steps I propose (happy to adjust):
1) I’ll send a one-page pricing snapshot + SOW draft for review (attached).
2) If the approver is in finance, suggest a 15-minute intro call I can run to walk pricing and procurement terms.
3) Tentative pilot kickoff week of Apr 11 if approvals clear.

Attachments: SOW-draft-v2.pdf (13KB), pricing-one-pager.pdf (8KB)

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0143

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@horizonhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from discovery — quick question on budget owner

Ben — thanks for the summary and the materials. Short answers:
- Primary approver will likely be our CFO, Dana Morales (dana.morales@horizonhealth.com).
- Procurement is involved for T&C but Dana signs budget approvals.
- Right now the budget window is "under review" — we are trying to decide which initiatives to prioritize for Q2 spend; Dana expects to finalize allocations by the last week of March, so end-of-quarter is still the likely decision milestone.

We need a simple pricing sheet for CFO review (she likes a single-page TCO view). Also, procurement might ask for a standard SOC2 attestation — can you confirm we can share SOC2 evidence / audit contact?

Happy to book a 15-min slot next week for a pricing walkthrough.

Alex
Alex Kim
Dir. Clinical Ops, HorizonHealth
alex.kim@horizonhealth.com | (415) 555-2290

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 14:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from discovery — quick question on budget owner

Appreciate the quick response, Alex — that's exactly what I needed. Two quick follow-ups:  
1) I'll send the one-page TCO you can hand to Dana (attached). It includes a conservative pilot estimate plus optional quantization/throughput knobs to lower cost if they need it.
2) SOC 2: yes — we can share our SOC 2 Type II report and a short security FAQ. I'll include a link and the contact for our compliance lead in the packet.

Would you prefer I send the packet to Dana directly or to you so you can route it? If it's easier, we can schedule a 15-min call next Tue (Mar 30) or Wed (Mar 31) — I can walk the CFO/procurement through pricing and the SOW.

On priority: is there any chance the decision window slips past end-of-quarter? Even a one-line pull (e.g., "will move to next cycle") helps us prioritize capacity and discount options.

Thanks — Ben

Alex — looping in case it's helpful: I've attached a one-page pricing snapshot that mirrors the TCO Ben mentioned and included a short SOC2 FAQ link below. Ben and I can join a 15-min call with Dana and procurement to walk the doc and note where pilot discounts apply.

SOC2 link: https://redwood.company/compliance/SOC2-summary-2027.pdf

If Dana is the primary approver, would you like us to send the packet directly to her or schedule a joint intro so you can participate? If the timeline shifts, we can also propose a phased pilot with a delayed billing start to align with budget windows.
